chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya, he raised it from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): Regarding

a man who ate the meat of game without knowing what it was, while he was in the state of ihram, he said: 'Upon him is the blood of a sheep.' And if two selves killed each other in the Haram, it is incumbent upon each one of them [to pay] blood money. Narrated.

key_terms.الْحَرَم: The sacred sanctuary, specifically referring to Mecca or Masjid al-Haram
key_terms.اِقْتَتَلَ: Mutually killed or fought until death
key_terms.دَمُ شَاةٍ: The blood money or expiation equivalent to the value of a sheep
key_terms.مُحْرِمٌ: One in the state of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for a pilgrim who accidentally eats game meat while in ihram?
ai.summary: In *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records Imam al-Sadiq (AS) specifying that accidental consumption of game by a muhrim incurs the penalty of a sheep's blood (*dam*), reflecting the juristic distinction between error and intent. The narration further establishes that in the sacred precincts, mutual homicide imposes individual liability for blood money on each party, underscoring the sanctity of the Haram and the precision of Shia fiqh in allocating financial compensation.
